rationale: PINS the #419 G3 gap: pattern type references — instanceof Point(int x, int y) (record pattern), instanceof String s (type pattern), and switch case Point(int x, int y) must each emit a reference to the pattern type. Previously the pattern type was silent (only the declared parameter type surfaced).

expectRelationships.note: CHANNEL pin for the pattern-type collector, on the QUALIFIED shape the analyzer can actually report. The rows above name the bare patterns (Point, String) and are unmet today, because the collector only emits a name containing a `.` - so nothing in the corpus observed the instanceof_expression / case_pattern channels at all, and dropping every one of them changed no verdict. `from` is left unconstrained on purpose: the collector sources a declared type at the enclosing class, which is exactly what the rows above dispute. This row asserts the edge exists, carries instanceof_expression, and names the line it is written on.
the SECOND qualified type pattern: one row per pattern, so losing the collector loses a row rather than hiding behind a surviving twin
the qualified SWITCH-case half. instanceof and case are separate walk cases in the analyzer, so they get separate rows: a regression that keeps one and drops the other cannot hide behind the survivor
